A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGP-Bench and Symbolic Instruction Tuning work. Text, tables, figures and appendices A–F support reliable comparison. Appendix content matches after accounting for renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, SIT experiments, general-reasoning evaluations, SGP-MNIST results and a human validation study, including supplementary experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds optical-illusion case studies involving OpenAI-o1 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

M1.justification: Section 3 adds a prompting-based inference variant: first translate an image into SVG, then answer using the generated program (Figures 5–6). This extends the demonstrated inference procedure; benchmark construction and SIT/rev-SIT training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds modified Ebbinghaus and Müller-Lyer scenarios testing relative circle size and line length despite familiar illusion cues. Existing SVG, CAD, SGP-MNIST, instruction-tuning and general-reasoning dataset coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The new illusion comparisons evaluate image-only answering against direct SVG answering and answering through an image-generated SVG. These introduce comparison procedures within the case studies; the model and comparator sets in the retained benchmark and SIT tables are unchanged.

E3.justification: Figures 5–6 introduce three input/prompt conditions for each illusion example. The indirect Claude prompt explicitly requests SVG translation without tools. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, perturbation settings, training budgets and appendix evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Two qualitative case studies are added to investigate whether symbolic representations mitigate errors associated with familiar visual illusions. Existing translation/rotation tests, prediction-entropy analysis and SIT ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing statistical reporting, including the human-study agreement statistics in Appendix B, is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results. New Figures 5–6 show OpenAI-o1 incorrectly calling unequal circles equal and Claude-3.5-Sonnet incorrectly calling unequal lines equal with image-only input; both give the correct ordering with supplied or generated SVG. These are added qualitative outcomes, not benchmark performance gains.

T1.justification: No formal definitions, assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are added or revised. The existing consistency formulation and SE(2) transformation setup are unchanged; arithmetic in the new examples is presented as model output.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about SGP-Bench, symbolic program understanding, SIT, SGP-MNIST difficulty and improvements in general reasoning.

C2.justification: Section 3 now interprets the retained Figure 4 as demonstrating actual reasoning rather than memorization. It also argues from the new illusion examples that SVG translation avoids spurious visual correlations. These are substantive interpretive extensions; existing discussions of failure conditions and SIT limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figures 5–6 supply new case-study prompts, SVG geometry and intermediate generated programs. Existing hardware descriptions, finetuning hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, evaluation templates and resource-access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 122 numbered reference entries are retained. Bibliographic differences concern citation page backreferences rather than added works or revised research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 3 receives a localized explanatory expansion, accompanied by small wording edits elsewhere and updated version headers. The overall section hierarchy, narrative structure and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 inserts two multipanel figures containing illusion images, prompts, SVG code and model responses. Nearby benchmark material moves and subsequent figures are renumbered; retained displays and appendix layouts are otherwise essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figures 5–6 add useful, inspectable examples of image-only errors and successful SVG-mediated answers while preserving the existing evidence. However, Section 3 also introduces stronger assertions about excluding memorization and eliminating spurious correlations that the displayed examples do not establish. The added illustrative value and less cautious interpretation have opposing effects, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
